evidence: WHAT APPLIES: the brief is interactive and time-varying (live board within 15 s without reload, preserving the open card, typed note and cursor; live conversation arrival while scrolled up or drafting; per-person unread counts and seen receipts; earlier-message paging that keeps place). It explicitly disclaims theming and phone layout (instruction.md: 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'), so no resize/toggle is owed; the template's polish responsive_layout (390x844) was correctly replaced, and visual/prompt.md line 14 says 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required.' Drag is optional in the brief and not graded. WHAT THE JUDGES ARE TOLD (strong): functional/prompt.md line 21 and polish/prompt.md line 18 define every 'within 15 seconds without reload' step as ONE browser_run_code_unsafe action: other person's step in an independent context, t0 only after triggerOk, DOM poll every 500 ms up to 15000 ms without clicking/typing/scrolling/reloading the observed page, return {triggerOk, met, ms}, void only if errored before t0 or the trigger failed, at most two repeats, a completed met=false is final, 2000 ms settle then read counts/focus/scroll/draft, and negative legs watched for the full 15000 ms then reload-confirmed (Colderwater lessons 7/14 satisfied). Report-every-step and skipped-step-fails (lesson 9): functional lines 23-25, polish lines 20-22. Modifier keys held during the click: app_context.md lines 33-35 (lesson 8). Criteria that exercise time/interaction rather than first paint: hro_live_board (V: Mei moves and adds, page read until both show), hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts (rise within 15 s, own messages never count, no rise while open at newest), hro_unread_scrolled_up (place not moved, notice, unread until viewed), hro_seen (Observer does not mark seen; Tomas/Bill/Rafael do, live), hro_thread_earlier (repeated paging with counts), hro_refused_put_back (document.activeElement after a refused move), hro_msg_compose (Shift+Enter/Enter, focus after send), hro_drafts (switch, Board, reload); polish hro_pol_live_board (open details, type note, scroll, live move, then details open / note text / activeElement / scroll offset / typing appends), hro_pol_live_thread (draft, focus, stay at newest on live arrival), hro_pol_earlier_place (getBoundingClientRect().top before/after paging), hro_pol_failed_send (route abort / setOffline), hro_pol_session_resume. Visual is an intentionally read-only craft review after opening details, the long conversation, Activity and the candidate view (visual/prompt.md line 14), appropriate for Likert craft. RESIDUAL ISSUES: (1) Sequencing ambiguity in polish hro_pol_live_board (polish/judge.toml, criterion hro_pol_live_board): it says type the unfinished note first, then scroll, and 'if neither scrolls at this viewport, add cards to that job through the ordinary controls until the page or the board scrolls', while polish/prompt.md line 24 recommends only 'open a job and add three cards' before this row. Adding cards after typing moves focus to the add form (and on a modal-details app may require closing the details), so a literal judge then sees the note not as document.activeElement or the details closed and fails a conforming app on a weight-2 row; nothing tells the judge to make the board scroll before opening details and typing. Whether the frozen golden page even scrolls with three cards at the judge's default playwright-mcp viewport is unmeasured (styles.css line 65: .board has no vertical overflow container; line 80: .detail is position: sticky; the scripted golden used 1440x900 / 1280x900 contexts, workspace.cjs lines 291, 308). (2) Missing runtime evidence: the scripted golden (workspace.json 'live board ... open card, note draft and focus kept', arrival_ms 810; 'conversation ... arrival while reading keeps draft, focus and scroll') never exercises the scroll-offset leg of hro_pol_live_board (workspace.cjs lines 378-395 read note value and activeElement only), and its at-newest arrival (workspace.cjs lines 465-468) runs with an empty composer, so the draft+focus+stay-at-newest combination of hro_pol_live_thread is not exercised. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'), so there is no evidence the GLM judge actually performs the single-action timed observations rather than separate tool calls; that is NOT EXERCISED, not a pass. No interactive promise is graded from a still first paint; the open items are a bounded procedural ambiguity and missing measurements.
counterexample: Conforming app whose board does not scroll with three cards at the judge viewport and whose add-candidate form sits on the board (or whose card details is a modal): following hro_pol_live_board literally, the judge opens details, types 'Call back on Fri', finds no scroll, adds cards through the form (focus moves to the form, or the modal closes), then after Mei's live move reads document.activeElement not on the note box or the details closed and scores 0 on a weight-2 polish row although the app preserves everything the brief asks. Conversely, a weak app that resets the board scroll on every poll can pass the scroll leg whenever the judge records 'cannot be made to scroll' and skips it.
suggested_fix: In hro_pol_live_board (and polish/prompt.md's 'workable order'), make the board scrollable first: add cards until the page or board scrolls (up to twelve), scroll it, and only then open a different card's details and type the note; then measure the golden at the judge's default viewport and add scripted golden legs for the scroll offset and for hro_pol_live_thread's draft-at-newest arrival.
